Hey there, I'm currently creating a D&D 5E campaign for my mates and I. I've pretty much done everything so far, even got a starting quest sorted for our first session in a week or two but I was wondering if you could provide any constructive criticism or suggestions on where to lead the campaign?

This is pretty much the backstory characters will hear when we start the campaign.

You were born in the land of Zorus, a world in its early stages of life. It’s only been a few hundred years since Zorus was formed by the two Gods, Pelor and Gruumsh. Pelor is the god of all that’s good in the world, whilst Gruumsh is the god of all that’s evil. Due to a conflict between the two gods on how the world should be run, a compromise was formed, Pelor would rule the Northen Lands, known as Pathiel, whilst Gruumsh would rule the South, known as Obrax. Both Gruumsh and Pelor also agreed a chosen one was to be selected from each kingdom to guide the people and represent each god in a physical form, each of these chosen ones gained astounding powers such as immortality, these two beings are known as ‘Pelor’s Chosen’ and ‘Gruumsh’s Chosen’. Before the two God’s departed Zorus to leave the world in the hands of the Chosen One’s, Pelor created a giant wall to separate the two kingdoms, this is known as ‘The Great Wall’.

So far the players will start the campaign just weeks after Pelor's chosen gets assassinated which opens the entire kingdom up for an eminent attack. After my player's starter quest they'll return to a village next to The Great Wall to find the village destroyed and in ruins with a huge breach in the Great Wall but before the players can react they get knocked unconscious from behind. I'm not sure where to lead the campaign from here, any ideas or suggestions would be appreciated.

The players might be expecting it to be the baddies who knock them unconscious, but perhaps it is a possible ally who was just trying to quickly take the party away from the breach. The way I see an attack like this would be that the wall was breached, and the first shock troops came, destroyed the village, and are now moving forward for reconnaissance, and the ally was dragging them away because the first large wave of troops was about to pass through the breach.

As time passes, you can figure out (either through the will of the die, or how you see fit) how the armies of the north and south are doing while the party does what they can to help the war effort. Since Pelor's chosen was assassinated, the southern armies probably have advantage on the demoralized northern armies.

Sounds like a really fun campaign, good luck gathering your ideas!

I like the side-choosing, but why not add in a few neutral factions as well to spice things up, such as spies, simple folk, or even cults? These could opt the players for some cool side-quests, while not-so-much continually looming on the fact that there are only the two warring factions.

Finding their way back to the kingdom-due to them being dragged relatively far away-may open up room for wood-based characters such as trackers, while also opening up opportunities for varying terrains.
